paths.description: Homepage and global chrome; represents the primary acquisition landing template.
Pricing/listing template; validates commercial clarity, locale pricing and responsive plan cards.
Product/detail template for Shopify Checkout; validates high-value feature communication.
Campaign landing template and primary conversion step before signup.
Primary signup handoff; secure admin endpoint presented a Cloudflare connection verification state to the audit browser.

findings.summary: The visual design is dark, but it does not respond to the user’s colour-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The CSS capability probe found no color-scheme declaration and no prefers-color-scheme rule; the emulated dark capture is the same fixed palette rather than a preference-driven theme.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light and dark tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Motion is not fully adapted for reduced-motion users.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the page still reported twelve running animations (nine at 400ms and three at 1000ms), while the CSS probe found no reduced-motion media rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a prefers-reduced-motion reduction layer that removes non-essential transitions and pauses decorative motion.

findings.summary: Page and state changes do not use declarative View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The rendered CSS capability probe found no view-transition rules across the homepage, despite navigation among multiple brochure routes.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document or cross-document View Transitions for route and major state changes, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: The animation-heavy page does not expose declarative scroll timelines.
findings.evidence: The CSS capability probe found no animation-timeline or scroll-timeline usage on a 12,000px homepage with extensive animated content.
findings.suggestedFix: Where motion is scroll-linked, replace scroll handlers with CSS scroll-driven animations and retain a static fallback.

findings.summary: The persistent cookie panel consumes scarce mobile viewport space.
findings.evidence: All four mobile screenshots show a fixed consent panel covering roughly the bottom 100px, including primary pricing and checkout content.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise the initial consent UI, keep choices equally prominent, and let users dismiss or defer it without obscuring core content.

findings.summary: The consent overlay is a custom role=dialog rather than a native dialog or popover.
findings.evidence: The semantic DOM probe found zero dialog, popover, or details elements and one role=dialog custom overlay.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a native dialog for modal consent details or a popover for transient controls, with platform focus and dismissal behaviour.

findings.summary: Cold-load mobile performance misses the fast-loading bar.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured FCP 4.8s, LCP 7.6s, TTI 7.6s and scored performance 0.62. The separate trace was faster (LCP 844ms), showing substantial run/network variance but not negating the poor cold-load result.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP request chain, prioritise the actual hero candidate, reduce initial JavaScript, and defer non-critical media and brochure modules.

findings.summary: The initial route has a heavy and complex delivery path.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 52 requests and 1,650,831 transferred bytes, including 28 scripts and 826,035 bytes attributed to fetch/XHR; Lighthouse also flagged the network dependency tree.
findings.suggestedFix: Shorten critical dependency chains, defer non-critical modules and requests, and verify each preload maps to an early critical consumer.

findings.summary: Some interactive controls lack reliable accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility scored 0.92 and failed aria-command-name, button-name, and label-content-name-mismatch; the DOM probe also found an empty 32x32 consent button without an aria-label.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every icon control a stable accessible name, align visible and accessible labels, and retest the full accessibility tree.

findings.summary: Consent controls include undersized touch targets.
findings.evidence: The focusable-control probe measured consent icon buttons at 32x32px. Lighthouse accessibility also identified control-name problems affecting non-pointer use.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase interactive hit areas to at least 44x44 CSS px and preserve a clearly visible focus indicator.

findings.summary: Image markup and delivery have avoidable quality gaps.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found 26 of 53 images without dimensions, 5 without srcset, 43 legacy-format assets, 2 oversized images and 42 missing alt attributes (some may be intentionally decorative).
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve intrinsic dimensions, use responsive sources and modern formats, and explicitly use empty alt only for decorative images.

findings.summary: The page uses a deprecated API and prevents back/forward cache restoration.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported one deprecated-API warning and one BFCache failure reason; best-practices scored 0.81.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the deprecated call and resolve the reported BFCache blocker, then verify navigation restoration in DevTools.

findings.summary: The main document lacks a Content-Security-Policy.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive confirmed HTTPS, HSTS and nosniff, but found no Content-Security-Policy. Cookies were Secure/SameSite=Lax and the secrets scan found no exposed credentials.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce- or hash-based CSP, starting in report-only mode, then enforce it after eliminating violations.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced defensive policies are absent.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors, no Referrer-Policy, and no Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Set frame-ancestors (or X-Frame-Options as legacy defence), strict Referrer-Policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Asset selection leaves measurable transfer-efficiency opportunities.
findings.evidence: The images primitive classified 43 of 53 image elements as legacy formats and found missing responsive sources; the route transferred 1.65MB on initial load.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve AVIF/WebP where beneficial, provide correctly sized srcsets, and avoid downloading hidden or non-critical decorative assets.
